lp.heroTitle: Make short clips feel finished fast.
lp.heroBody: Filmtone is a desktop-first finisher for short-form video. Try the look on your own media in the browser, then finish and export on macOS with dependable playback, compare, and signature character. Keep stills in the same world when you need matching covers or supporting frames.
lp.heroSecondaryLine: Apple Silicon · macOS {minMacos}+ — full requirements on the download page.
lp.proofTeaserLine: Play it, compare it, finish it.
lp.heroProofBody: A proof cut from a real graded clip. Let the finished feel land in motion before the page asks you to think about controls or release details.
lp.surfaceSplitTitle: Try the look on web. Finish on Desktop.
lp.surfaceSplitWebBody: Open your own frame or short clip, compare in motion, and decide whether the tone is heading in the right direction.
lp.surfaceSplitDesktopBody: Finish and export on macOS when you need dependable playback, compare, Cross Filter, and a workflow you can trust on real footage.
lp.expandAuxiliaryPanelsTitle: Show more: fine controls, LUT, compare, histogram, save…
lp.expandAuxiliaryPanelsHint: Skip this if presets and the Quick sliders are enough.
lp.valueTitle: Why macOS helps you keep tone consistent
lp.valueBullet1: Carry one look across many stills with the same feel.
lp.valueBullet2: Process a folder of photos into another folder with a cohesive finish—and nudge one short clip to match when you need it.
lp.valueBullet3: Try the vibe here first, then finish and deliver from the macOS app.
lp.workflowTitle: Bring the same world into stills.
lp.workflowLead: Stills matter here as a companion surface, not a separate product identity.
lp.workflowBullet1: Use stills for covers, thumbnails, gallery frames, and supporting images around the clip.
lp.workflowBullet2: Keep the mood consistent instead of rebuilding it in a separate photo-first workflow.
lp.workflowBullet3: Treat the clip as the center of gravity, then extend that same world outward when you need it.
lp.demoEyebrow: Try your own media on web
lp.demoTitle: Audition a look in the browser
lp.demoBody: Open a frame or short clip, start from the core controls, and compare in motion. When you want dependable finishing and export, move to the macOS app.
lp.demoStatusAria: Current media source and split preview state
lp.faqAfree: Yes. Both the browser and desktop versions are free. There is an optional support mechanism, but it does not unlock extra features.
lp.faqQformats: What kind of media can I try here?
lp.faqAformats: In the browser, open a photo or short video clip to audition the look. On Desktop, move to the stronger production path when you need finishing and export on macOS.
lp.faqQwhichVersion: Should I use the browser or the desktop app?
lp.faqAwhichVersion: Use the browser to try the look on your own media and compare quickly. Use the macOS app when you're ready to finish, export, and trust the result on real footage.
lp.faqQpresets: Is Filmtone just a preset pack?
lp.faqApresets: No. Presets are only the starting point. Filmtone is about getting to a finished feel quickly through playback judgment, trust, and signature finish.
lp.faqAvideo: Yes. Stills matter as a same-world extension for covers, thumbnails, gallery frames, and supporting images around the clip.
lp.faqAwindows: The desktop app is macOS-only (Apple Silicon). The browser version works on any OS.
lp.premiumCapabilitiesTitle: See the finish land in motion.
lp.premiumFeature1Body: This is a real graded low-light clip. Colored lights bloom, the frame stops feeling raw, and the finished feel shows up before any product UI has to explain itself.
lp.premiumFeature2Body: A second real graded clip in a different lighting setup. The point is not one hero shot, but that the current shipped finish already carries recognizable character across motion.
lp.premiumGridTitle: The shipped surface is getting safer to judge.
lp.premiumCard1Body: Play, scrub, compare, and review quickly. Playback judgment is part of the product, not a side note.
lp.premiumCard2Body: Progressive preview and reusable proxies keep real camera files workable instead of blocking the finish.
lp.premiumCard3Body: In v1.0, Cross Filter runs live on the WebGPU preview path, with inline threshold, chromatic, and spacing controls.
lp.premiumCard4Body: Desktop is built to finish short-form video first, then carry that mood into stills, covers, and supporting frames.
lp.premiumCompareTitle: Show the shipped surface on a real compare pass.
lp.premiumCompareBody: These silent macOS captures are product proof, not mood reels. They show playback, compare, and finish judgment on actual footage.
lp.premiumCompareCard1Body: A current desktop capture showing before/after judgment on a real night clip while the footage keeps moving.
lp.premiumCompareCard2Body: A brighter shot where compare remains readable in motion and Cross Filter decisions can be checked before export.
lp.premiumCompareCard3Body: A moodier low-light clip to reinforce trust before export, even when the footage is less forgiving than a hero shot.

controls.bloomToggleHint: Soft glow that spreads from bright areas (bloom).
controls.bloomThresholdHint: Only pixels brighter than this level contribute strongly to the glow.
controls.halationToggleHint: Colored glow around very bright edges (halation).
controls.finishToolsMistOutcome: Soften the whole image with a finished haze.
controls.finishToolsCrossOutcome: Turn point lights into a visible optical signature.
controls.finishToolsTextureOutcome: Add grain and falloff to make the image feel finished.
controls.finishToolsLensOutcome: Add subtle fringing and softness to break the digital clean edge.
controls.finishToolsMotionOutcome: Shape motion smear and trails while you judge in playback.
controls.artifactsSectionHint: Grain, vignette, glow, halation, and related film-look controls.
controls.sourceTrimSectionHint: Adjust the imported image before the film look—exposure, color, highlights, and shadows.
controls.compressionHint: Softens bright tones with a film-style shoulder curve. Not file or data compression.
controls.compressionRangeHint: Widens or narrows how much of the tonal range that softness affects (highlights through shadows).
controls.printContrastHint: Adds contrast in the print-style stage—separate from the main Contrast slider in the grading stack.
controls.rgbShiftToggleHint: Turn chromatic aberration on or off. It can break the image if pushed too far, so use it only when needed.
controls.grainRadialMixHint: Near 0: even grain. Near 1: stronger toward frame edges (not chromatic aberration). At 1 matches the previous default.
controls.lightShaftsToggleHint: Volumetric beams of light radiating from a point in the frame.
controls.shaftIntensityHint: Overall brightness of the light shafts. Zero means off.
controls.shaftDecayHint: How quickly the beams fade as they spread from the source.
controls.shaftOriginXHint: Horizontal position of the light source (0 = left, 1 = right).
controls.shaftOriginYHint: Vertical position of the light source (0 = top, 1 = bottom).
controls.crossFilterToggleHint: Star-shaped light streaks from bright points, like a physical cross-screen lens filter.
controls.crossFilterSpikesHint: Number of light spikes: 4-point (classic cross), 6-point (snow cross), or 8-point (sunny cross).
controls.crossFilterAngleHint: Rotates the spike pattern. 0° places the first spike pointing right.
controls.crossFilterLengthHint: How far the light spikes extend from bright sources.
controls.crossFilterThresholdHint: Only pixels brighter than this level produce spikes. Higher values limit the effect to the brightest points.
controls.crossFilterChromaticHint: Color dispersion along each spike, like light diffracting through a ruled grating.
controls.crossFilterSizeLimitHint: Suppresses streaks from large light sources. Higher values limit the effect to small point sources, excluding lamps, sun, or other area lights.
controls.crossFilterRandomnessHint: Controls what fraction of light sources produce streaks. Lower values create a sparse, selective effect.
controls.crossFilterHardModeOverrideHint: Hard Mode forces these values internally. Switch to Soft to control them manually.
controls.crossFilterMinSpacingHint: Reduces the intensity of nearby overlapping streaks while preserving the light cluster shape. Use this to declutter dense groups such as chandeliers.
controls.dustAmountHint: Adds random dust particles over the image, like aged film stock.
controls.scratchAmountHint: Adds vertical film scratches that drift across the frame.
controls.trailIntensityHint: Extends the motion trail beyond the shutter window. Higher values create longer afterimages.

batch.tipExportTabIntro: Photos in a folder can be saved in bulk to another folder with your Filmtone look. You can also export one video as MP4 with the same look. After adjusting sliders on Edit, use “Send grade to Export” (bottom right) to copy values here. LUTs are separate (e.g. load JSON).
batch.tipJobImages: Every .jpg / .jpeg / .png in the chosen folder gets this look, saved as JPEG or PNG to another folder.
batch.tipJobVideoFastOption: Default is fast one-pass ffmpeg (approximate). Turn on step-by-step WebGL only if you want a closer match to the preview. .cube LUT is preferred; Params are approximated in ffmpeg — lutIntensity, bloom, halation, and split-tone details may not match. ffmpeg and ffprobe must be on PATH.
batch.tipJobVideoWebGlOnly: Only WebGL frame-by-frame export (slower) for a closer preview match. Fast one-pass ffmpeg is being prepared and hidden from the UI. ffmpeg and ffprobe must be on PATH.
batch.tipSourcesImagesFolder: Only .jpg / .jpeg / .png in that folder (not subfolders by default in UI copy). Not for video conversion.
batch.tipSourcesVideoFile: Import limit: up to 4K and max {maxSec}s. ffmpeg and ffprobe must be on PATH.
batch.tipLookJsonDetails: Use when passing or saving a full look (including LUT) as a file. Usually “Send grade to Export” or preset is enough.
batch.tipApplyEditGradeToBatch: Copies slider and tone values from Edit into this export (same as “Send grade to Export”). After changing preset, preset values apply until you sync. LUT (.cube) is not copied here — use “Advanced: Grade JSON” below.
batch.tipFilenameSuffix: Inserted before the extension. Example: -graded → IMG0001-graded.jpg. Empty = no suffix. Use a different folder than sources to avoid overwriting.
batch.tipVideoOutputNaming: Output file name is original stem + -graded.mp4. Max output FHD · {fps} fps.
batch.tipWebglAccurate: When on, seeks each frame and grades via readPixels — very slow but closest to Edit. Off (default) uses fast ffmpeg one-pass (approximate). .cube LUT preferred; Params approximated in ffmpeg.
batch.tipKeyboardShortcuts: ⌘1 / ⌘2 (Ctrl on Windows) switch tabs. On Export, ⌘↵ runs “{imagesLabel}” or “Export video”. ⇧⌘↵ retries failed items only (photos). ⇧⌘Y resumes. Esc cancels.
batch.tipDesktopPrefsPersist: Input/output folders become defaults next time (existing paths). Window position and size are saved on quit.
batch.tipResumeSession: Continue with saved I/O and look for remaining frames only. Discard removes the record only — already exported files stay on disk.

quickProFilmStock040.description: Quick stays on the shortest path; Pro exposes process, artifacts, source trim, and LUT in order. Preset surfaces group film stocks with clearer boundaries (including stocks like Velvia 50).

videoTransport042.title: Video preview transport (v0.4.2)
videoTransport042.description: Play/pause, timeline scrub, timecode, and Space to toggle playback on Web and Desktop — with locks during export or preview hold, and safe interaction alongside Compare mode.

proPanelVocabulary042.title: Pro panel vocabulary & inline hints (v0.4.2)
proPanelVocabulary042.description: Clearer Pro labels (film texture, source adjustments, color fringing), improved Japanese for Bloom/Halation, hover hints on collapsible headers, and a Bloom threshold tooltip.

fasterVideoExport043.title: Faster export for heavy codec sources (v0.4.3)
fasterVideoExport043.description: 4K HEVC and other heavy format sources are automatically optimized before export, delivering up to 4× faster throughput.

progressivePreview051.title: Progressive preview for heavy footage (v0.5.1)
progressivePreview051.description: Heavy formats such as ProRes and 4K HEVC now open with an immediate native-decoded preview, then switch over to an optimized intermediate in the background for smoother work.

portraitMotionBlur051.title: Portrait video + rebuilt motion blur (v0.5.1)
portraitMotionBlur051.description: Vertical footage now displays in full-frame contain mode, and motion blur has been rebuilt around an eight-frame ring buffer with shutter-angle control.

crossFilter060.title: Cross Filter optical effect (v0.6.0)
crossFilter060.description: A new diffraction-style star filter for bright point lights, with controls for strength, point count, rotation, streak length, threshold, and chromatic split.

proxyCacheAndVideoUx060.title: Proxy cache and video UX polish (v0.6.0)
proxyCacheAndVideoUx060.description: Desktop now keeps progressive preview proxies in a bounded local cache, while compare dismissal, faster playback review, slider reset discoverability, and thumbnail/loading polish have all been improved.

desktopPolish061.title: Desktop stability and look polish (v0.6.1)
desktopPolish061.description: The launch-time update banner is back, preview recovery after export is more reliable, glow was retuned for black-mist night scenes, and hard cross-filter spacing now behaves more predictably.

crossFilterCleanup062.title: Cross Filter product-surface cleanup (v0.6.2)
crossFilterCleanup062.description: The public product surface now freezes Soft mode, normalises restored and shared state back to Hard, and replaces the old Spikes slider with direct 4 / 6 / 8 choices.

webgpuPreview100.title: Desktop v1.0 — WebGPU preview backend
webgpuPreview100.description: Desktop preview now runs on a WebGPU path with wider highlight headroom, and Cross Filter ships live on that preview path with inline threshold, chromatic, and spacing controls.

presetExpansion.title: Preset expansion
presetExpansion.description: Additional film stocks and creative looks beyond the initial four.

exportQuality.title: Preview/export parity for video and batch
exportQuality.description: Bring video export and batch output closer to the new WebGPU preview path so highlight rolloff and overall rendering match more reliably.

verticalVideoExportQuality.title: Portrait & non-16:9 video export resolution
verticalVideoExportQuality.description: Improving scaling so vertical sources are less likely to be shrunk more than needed, using a long-edge-oriented cap.

smartLookAi.title: Smart Look AI
smartLookAi.description: AI-assisted image correction on Desktop — adjusts photos to better suit the chosen preset's look. Desktop-first; Web may follow later.

dngRawSupport.title: DNG / RAW support
dngRawSupport.description: Import and grade raw files directly without prior conversion.

windowsSupport.title: Windows support
windowsSupport.description: Bring Filmtone Desktop to Windows for broader accessibility.

lutExport.title: LUT export
lutExport.description: Export your grade as a .cube LUT for use in DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, and other editors.

filmDeveloperFuture.title: Film-style develop step (under evaluation)
filmDeveloperFuture.description: Exploring whether a dedicated develop-style stage fits Filmtone. Not included in v0.4; timing and scope are TBD.

mobileApp.title: Mobile app
mobileApp.description: A lightweight mobile companion for quick grading on the go.

cloudSync.title: Cloud preset sync
cloudSync.description: Sync your custom presets across Desktop, Web, and Mobile.

pluginIntegration.title: Editor plugin integration
pluginIntegration.description: Integrate Filmtone presets directly into photo and video editing apps.

releaseNotes.title: Release Notes — Filmtone
releaseNotes.description: Filmtone Desktop release history — see what's new, fixed, and improved in each version.
releaseNotes.heroBody: Every Filmtone Desktop release, from the very first build to today. Each entry covers what was added, what was improved, and what was fixed.

entries.v100Title: Filmtone Desktop v1.0 — the first public release
entries.v100WebgpuPreview: Preview has been reworked end-to-end. Bright highlights now hold their shape more naturally, so it is easier to judge the finished look right on screen.
entries.v100CrossFilterPreviewControls: Cross Filter now responds live while you preview your image. Fine-tune the brightness that triggers the streaks, how much they split into color, and how close they sit, and the result updates immediately.
entries.v100SignedNotarizedDmg: The macOS build is now signed and notarized by Apple. The download page and the in-app update prompt both point to this v1.0.0 release, so installing is simple and trusted.
entries.v100DesktopFirstReleaseScope: v1.0 focuses on improving Desktop preview. The browser demo, video export, and photo batch export continue to work exactly as they did before.
entries.v062HardOnlySurface: Cross Filter now ships as a single, well-tuned mode, trimmed down so it is easier to reach for without hesitation.
entries.v062StateNormalization: Old settings files and shared links open correctly and automatically fit into the current mode — nothing looks different from what you originally saved.
entries.v062DiscreteSpikes: Pick the number of streaks in one tap: 4, 6, or 8.
entries.v061Title: Update notifications are back, and night-scene glow feels better
entries.v061LaunchUpdateBanner: Filmtone again shows a banner at launch when a newer version is available.
entries.v061PreviewRecoveryAfterExport: Fixed cases where preview could stay black after exporting — preview now recovers on its own whenever it is needed.
entries.v061GlowBlackMistRetune: Glow in Black-Mist-style night scenes now keeps its shape instead of flattening into blown-out white patches.
entries.v061HardCrossFilterSpacing: Cross Filter streaks now separate cleanly even when bright highlights sit close together.
entries.v060Title: Cross Filter arrives, and video feels smoother
entries.v060CrossFilter: Cross Filter adds lens-style star streaks to bright points in your image. Dial in the strength, the number of streaks, the angle, the length, the brightness that triggers them, and a touch of color split, to find your own look.
entries.v060VideoCompareUx: Video compare and review feel smoother — compare mode is easier to exit, slider resets are easier to find, and a faster playback option makes quick checks more natural.
entries.v060ThumbnailLoadingPolish: Leading thumbnails now pick a brighter frame automatically, so clips that fade in look right from the very first glance. Loading text has also been aligned with the rest of the app.
entries.v060PersistentProxyCache: Desktop can now keep preview data for heavy footage on your computer, so opening the same clip again is faster. You can let Filmtone manage the space automatically or clear it yourself whenever you want.
entries.v051ProgressiveLoading: ProRes, 4K HEVC, and other demanding formats preview the moment you drop them in. Filmtone prepares an optimized copy in the background and reuses it at export, so you never wait on the same clip twice.
entries.v051RingBufferMotionBlur: Motion blur has been rebuilt with real shutter-angle control (0° to 720°), and a separate Trail Intensity slider for stylised streaks, so you can shape the look more intuitively.
entries.v051PortraitVideo: 9:16 vertical clips now display full-frame. The side areas are filled with a softly blurred version of the footage itself, so portrait video looks polished without any manual setup.
entries.v051ComparisonModeFix: Fixed Before / After compare so only the graded side shows motion blur — the original stays clean, and no ghost frames carry over when you switch modes.
entries.v050Title: Grain that looks like the real thing
entries.v050GrainV3: The grain engine has been rebuilt from the ground up — each film stock now has its own natural clumping, texture size, and color-noise character, so Kodak and Fuji grain no longer look the same.
entries.v050Diffusion: A new Diffusion slider wraps your image in a soft, milky haze — like shooting through a Pro-Mist filter — gently lifting contrast and flattering skin tones.
entries.v050CineStillHalation: CineStill 800T now loads clean by default. Dial in the iconic red halation glow yourself with the slider whenever you want it.
entries.v050PresetRecalibration: All 10 film stock presets have been hand-tuned with matching grain size and diffusion, so each look feels true to the actual film it was inspired by.
entries.v050UiReorganization: The Pro panel has been reorganized so the controls you use most are immediately visible. Effects still being refined are tucked away until they are ready.
entries.v045BloomHalationRework: Bloom and halation have been completely reimagined — glow spreads more naturally, highlights behave at any slider position, and the overall look is closer to real film. Existing grades may shift slightly.
entries.v045PresetRecalibration: All 10 film stock presets have been recalibrated so bloom and halation feel natural and true to each stock's character.
entries.v044ProresLoadAndExport: You can now import, grade, and export ProRes MOV files — including LOG footage straight from your camera. Filmtone prepares the file automatically on the way in.
entries.v044Dci4kInput: Cinema-resolution files (DCI 4K and above) are now fully supported as video input.
entries.v043FasterHevcExport: 4K footage that used to take three minutes to export now finishes in under 45 seconds — up to 4× faster for demanding camera files.
entries.v043AutoSourceOptimize: Filmtone quietly optimizes heavy camera files before grading so export runs at full speed. Lighter files skip this step entirely.
entries.v043OptimizationProgress: A progress bar now shows while Filmtone prepares a heavy source file, so you know exactly what is happening before export begins.
entries.v042ProPanelVocabulary: Pro panel labels have been updated to plain photography language — Film texture, Color fringing, Source adjustments — so controls are easier to understand at a glance.
entries.v042BloomThresholdHint: Bloom's threshold slider now shows a brief tip explaining which highlight tones trigger the glow.
entries.v042VideoTransport: Video preview now has full playback controls — play, pause, scrub, timecode display, and Space bar toggle.
entries.v041ProToneLabels: The tone section now uses everyday language — highlight softness, tone span, print snap — with short hover descriptions so every slider is self-explanatory.
entries.v041SliderTooltipReset: All sliders now show a tip reminding you that tapping the label resets that control to default.
entries.v040Title: Film process controls and a cleaner workflow
entries.v040FilmProcess: New film process controls let you shape compression, tonal range, print contrast, and color cast — what you see in the preview is exactly what exports.
entries.v040QuickProIa: Quick mode takes you straight to the look; Pro mode surfaces the full set of film process, texture, and source controls — each mode shows only what you need.
entries.v040FilmStockPicker: Film stocks are now grouped by category, so finding Velvia 50 among cinematic and other options takes seconds instead of scrolling.
entries.v040PanelStability: Desktop no longer loses your process settings when you switch between photo and video tabs.
entries.v040ShareCompat: Shared links and exported grades remain fully compatible with older versions while carrying the new process fields when available.
entries.v031Title: Export in the browser — and better reliability across the board
entries.v031WebVideoExportBeta: You can now export a graded video clip directly from the browser — no download required to test your look on short footage.
entries.v031WebBrowserReliability: Browser export is more reliable, and a clearer message now guides Safari users toward Chrome, Edge, or the Desktop app when needed.
entries.v031FinderThumb: Exported MP4s no longer show a black thumbnail in Finder or Quick Look — previews now display the actual graded frame.
entries.v031MovHandling: Video import now handles a wider range of camera files, including MOV files that some cameras save without standard type information.
entries.v030Title: Cleaner export and faster preset discovery
entries.v030ExportIa: Photo batch export and single video export are now clearly separated — tabs, panel, and toolbar all point you to the right place.
entries.v030ExportSource: The image or clip you are actively grading carries over into export as the default, so wrong-file exports are much less likely.
entries.v030VisualPolish: The export panel and the editing view share the same visual language, making the transition between grading and exporting feel seamless.
entries.v030PresetSearch: Type to search film stock presets — no more scrolling through the full list to find a specific look.
entries.v030ExportBusyPause: Video preview pauses automatically while a file is exporting so nothing looks out of sync.
entries.v030WebPreview: The browser demo preview is taller and better framed, giving a closer impression of the Desktop experience.
entries.v020Title: Two LUTs at once, redesigned export, and faster video
entries.v020DualLut: Load two LUT files simultaneously — use the first to convert your LOG footage to a standard look, the second for your creative grade, each with its own intensity control.
entries.v020LutSync: LUTs you set in the editing tab now follow through to export. A status indicator shows at a glance whether your grade is in sync, out of sync, or partially applied.
entries.v020InlineExportPanel: Export now lives right alongside your grade in a compact panel — the image stays visible the whole time, no more multi-step wizard.
entries.v020WebCodecsReEnabled: Video export in the browser has been restored with improved color accuracy and hardware-accelerated performance.
entries.v020UpdateNotify: A banner appears inside the app when a new version of Filmtone is available.
entries.v020PackageRefactor: Under-the-hood restructuring to keep the app fast and stable as new features are added.
entries.v013FrameLogSuppression: Video export now runs more cleanly in the background, with a small performance improvement on longer clips.
entries.v012VideoColorShift: Fixed a color shift that could appear in exported video, ensuring graded footage matches what you see on screen.
entries.v011FfmpegPath: Fixed an issue where the Desktop app (DMG) could fail to process video after installation.
entries.v010BatchExport: Apply any preset to an entire folder of photos and export them all at once as JPEG or PNG.
entries.v010VideoExport: Export a short video clip with your chosen grade baked in.
entries.v010FourPresets: Four film stock looks to start: Kodak Portra 400, Fuji Pro 400H, Kodak Ektar 100, and Ilford HP5 Plus.
entries.v010BrowserDemo: Try any preset on your own photos in the browser before downloading the Desktop app.

metadata.title: Filmtone iPhone Privacy
metadata.description: Privacy summary for Filmtone on iPhone: local-first operation, no account, no analytics SDK, no third-party tracking, and no data collection.

privacyPage.heroBody: Filmtone on iPhone is local-first. The app does not require an account, does not include analytics or third-party tracking SDKs, and does not collect your photos, videos, or usage data.

facts.localFirstValue: Editing, preview, and export run on your device.
facts.noAccountValue: No sign-in, no profile, no cloud sync requirement.
facts.noAnalyticsValue: No analytics SDK. No ad-tech SDK.
facts.noCollectionValue: No collected data types. No third-party tracking.

localFirst.title: Editing stays on your iPhone
localFirst.body: This release keeps the media workflow on device. The app is designed to work without an account or cloud processing.

editing.title: Editing runs locally
editing.body: Applying looks, generating previews, and exporting media happen on the iPhone itself.

storage.title: Working files stay on device
storage.body: The app may keep local working files and current settings on your device so the current session can continue.

server.title: No media upload for grading
server.body: The iPhone release does not send your selected photos or videos to our server for preview, grading, or export.

permissions.title: Photo Library permission is used only for import and save
permissions.body: Permissions are requested only when the related feature is used.

photoImport.title: Photo Library import
photoImport.body: Photo Library access is requested only when you choose to import from Photo Library.

photoSave.title: Save to Photos
photoSave.body: Photo Library add access is requested only when you choose Save to Photos for an export.

files.title: Files import
files.body: If you choose Files, iOS gives the app only the item you selected.

tracking.title: No analytics SDK, no third-party tracking
tracking.body: The public iPhone release does not use analytics or third-party tracking.

items.noTracking: No third-party tracking or tracking domains.
items.noCollection: No data collection by the app.

contact.title: Questions about privacy
contact.body: Questions about this privacy page or a specific release behavior can be sent to {operatorName} by email.

about.title: About
about.description: Takumi Chiba — full-stack engineer, creative director, photographer, marketing strategist, bilingual communicator. Five practices, one studio.

journal.title: Journal
journal.description: Notes on works, technical writing, and motion-study archives.
journal.intro: Notes from behind the work — production thinking, technical writing, and motion-study archives held under one craft bar across code, motion, film, and photography.

motionStudies.title: Motion Studies
motionStudies.intro: Named techniques pulled into narrow reference works, each held against its own runtime truth and a specific benchmark.

signalStrokeRelay.title: Signal Stroke Relay
signalStrokeRelay.summary: Lead line, icon, title, and underline relayed through trim paths, staggered offsets, and a deliberate match cut.

anchoredProgressResolve.title: Anchored Progress Resolve
anchoredProgressResolve.summary: A progress bar held as a state machine — anchored fill, blink channel, and a deliberate resolve state in browser SVG + DOM.

boilingPosterAperture.title: Boiling Poster Aperture
boilingPosterAperture.summary: Boiling edges, mask gates, and displacement-led reveals on a single PixiJS poster — built so the reveal stays the main event.

motifLoopBackground.title: Motif Loop Background
motifLoopBackground.summary: A motif-driven looping background that breathes without competing with the foreground — loop phasing held inside a safety clamp.

stagedEmphasisPayoff.title: Staged Emphasis Payoff
stagedEmphasisPayoff.summary: A title sequence broken into graphemes that stack, hand off emphasis, and release on a deliberate hold — built on browser SVG + DOM.

temporalEchoResidue.title: Temporal Echo Residue
temporalEchoResidue.summary: Lyric and glyph residue stacked from time-offset samples, gated by alpha decay — a PixiJS reference for trail and echo grammar.

experiments.title: Experiments
experiments.description: Motion works built from WebGPU and sound — prototypes that hold visual, tactile, and temporal grip in code.
experiments.intro: A working studio for sensing texture, time, and sound through code — sitting upstream of Filmtone and Journal.

dot.title: Motion Dot
dot.concept: A dot field that finds form through accumulation. WebGPU plus audio input — a study in handling density and time.

grid.title: Motion Grid
grid.concept: A grid of cells, breathing and breaking under audio and gesture — rhythm carved by structure itself.

flow.title: Motion Flow
flow.concept: Fluid lines that read time as a continuous gesture — flow as a way of seeing.
